paper.title: Terrain Generation Using Procedural Models Based on Hydrology
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Graphics, 32(4), Article 143 (Proceedings of SIGGRAPH 2013)

relevant_section_or_figure: Figure 2; Section 6.2, Terrain Primitives Generation; Section 7, Terrain Tree Definition.
transferable_principle: Construct world form hierarchically from a sparse macro-structure that partitions the domain, then synthesize local detail as compact-support primitives combined by explicit blend, replace, and carve operators. Let detail inherit scale and boundaries from the macro-structure instead of applying uniform noise everywhere.
application_to_world_v21: Derive a sparse world-structure graph from the live snapshot: nodes are major task parcels or state-transition hubs, and edges are active parcel adjacency or worker flow. Use that graph to define a small number of broad terrain/material regions and landmark bands, with per-region detail and geometry budgets. Bind state markers to graph regions and reserve negative space around them; keep worker traces and receipts as local detail so macro relief establishes scale while semantic states remain readable.
falsifier: Render the same snapshot with the current flat/noise-plus-clutter pipeline and with the graph-partitioned construction-tree pipeline at matched camera, object count, and palette. If blinded reviewers cannot more reliably identify world scale and epistemic/task states, or if readability gains disappear when geometry density is held constant, the principle is falsified for v21.
fake_evidence: No World v21 improvement is claimed from the paper. The paper supports the hierarchical construction-tree and primitive-composition method only; its hydrologic assumptions, examples, performance figures, and visual results must not be presented as evidence that graph-derived task terrain improves v21.
